## Patrol reading — still RED on `main` ~12½ hours later, same signature, now on a NEWER release candidate

`domain:devx` execution PM seat (#6023), session `session_012GKcPZbMoGq7WPzKLfRBTU`. ⛔ **Not claiming and not reassigning** — this card is dispatched and `os-bill` holds it. Recording a measurement because this is the lane's surface and `main` is still red.

### The red is unbroken

Four consecutive `Packed-tarball smoke (release candidate)` failures on `main`, most recent **13:32Z**:

| run | head | conclusion |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [34357711815](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34357711815) 13:32Z | `44c917a47a` | **failure** |

| [34349986006](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/34349986006) 12:15Z | `9cdffbe365` | **failure** |

The card records the run starting ~01:07Z. ⇒ unbroken for roughly **12½ hours**, across at least ten distinct `main` heads, still posting `publish-smoke / packed-tarballs` = `failure` with *"Release candidate fails a fresh install"*.

### ⭐ Same signature — and it has now survived a release-candidate version bump

The card measured this on **17.4.0** tarballs. Run `34357711815` is on **17.5.0**:

```
at async _SqlDriver.create (…/@objectstack+driver-sql@file+..+tarballs+objectstack-driver-sql-17.5.0.tgz/…)
at async _ObjectQL.createWithAutonumberResync (…/objectstack-objectql-17.5.0.tgz/…)
ERROR Insert operation failed {"object":"sys_oauth_resource","error":{"message":
  "UNIQUE constraint failed: sys_oauth_resource.identifier …"}}
##[error]error-level log lines during BOOT, before any probe ran (see above)
```

⇒ ⛔ Not an artifact of one candidate build. Same object, same constraint, same two frames, one minor version later.

### ⭐ New reading the card lists as NOT MEASURED: the boot is HEALTHY

The card says *"No probe ever ran"* and leaves the boot's own verdict open. The `server.log` tail in this run answers it:

```
  Plugins: 34 loaded
           ObjectQL, SqlDriver, …, Auth, …, DatasourceAdminRoutes
  ✓ Server is ready
  ➜  API:       http://localhost:3210/
  healthy after probe #4 — our server is on port 3210
```

⇒ The server **booted, loaded all 34 plugins including `Auth`, and answered its health probe**. The job then died at the scan. That strengthens the card's own hypothesis 1 — *"the scan's population is wrong, not its severity"* — from "most likely" toward measured: a run whose boot demonstrably succeeded is being reported as a failed boot.

⚠️ Still ⛔ NOT measured, and I did not measure it either: whether the auth + CRUD probes pass. They still never execute.

### ⭐ And the runtime already draws the distinction the scan does not

Two lines below the fatal one, from the same boot, the app's own diagnostics block:

```
  ⚠ Boot diagnostics — 1 warning logged during startup:
    … WARN [Analytics] No admitObjectRead configured …
```

⇒ The runtime separates warnings from errors and reports the count. There is also a second `[sql-driver] DATABASE_ERROR` line in the same boot (`no such table: _objectstack_sequences`) that the scan does **not** trip on. So the scan is already selective — it is picking exactly one caught exception's ERROR line out of a boot it otherwise tolerates. ⚠️ I have not read the scan's predicate to establish *why* that one and not the other; that is the taker's, and it may be the fastest route to hypothesis 1.

### What I am asking for, and from whom

⛔ Nothing from this seat's authority. This is `os-bill`'s card, PR **#17051** is open on `claude/issue-17027-boot-error-scan` (branch still present on the remote; the fix is **not** on `main` — `scripts/publish-smoke.sh` there has **0** `sys_oauth_resource` mentions, so no ignore-list shortcut has landed either).

⇒ Flagging only that the cost is still accruing: the release this holds is the one open action on **#16500**, and the published on-ramp stays broken for new users while it waits. ⚠️ **A red on `main` that is 12½ hours old and still posting a commit status is past the point where it should be discovered by patrol rather than reported by its owner.**

## Awaiting a maintainer decision — the gate-strength trade-off in PR #17051, recorded here rather than left in chat

⛔ **A conclusion that lives only in a chat session is a half-state.** These options were put to the maintainer in session `session_019wtfW1ZxGnP1XKGc9uZVms` and are written here so they survive it. ⚠️ **No decision has been made yet** — nothing below is approved.

### What #17051 changes about gate strength

| judged at boot | before #16976 | #16976 (lived 5h) | PR #17051 |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| composition-arrival predicate | — | **fails** | **fails** (untouched) |
| named signatures (#3091's line) | — | — | **fails** (new allow-list) |
| any error-level line | — | **fails** ← the false positive | **prints, does not fail** |
| section 4 (after probes) | whole log | whole log | **probe window only** |

### The cell that needs a ruling

An error-level line in the **boot window** that is neither a composition-arrival failure nor on the named allow-list:

- **before #16976** — section 4's whole-log rescan caught it ⇒ red
- **after #17051** — printed, not fatal, and section 4 no longer reaches it ⇒ **passes**

⇒ Measured against the long-standing baseline this is a **real coverage reduction**, not purely a false-positive repair. That places it on the 人工地板 「门禁削弱」 line, which is why the dispatching seat is not deciding it.

### Why the delivered shape was forced, not chosen

⭐ The seat's own suggested route (narrow the boot gate only) was **measured false** by the dev: `SMOKE_ERROR_LOG_PATTERN` was applied in **two** places and the boot window is a prefix of the whole log, so neutering only the boot check left the run red at section 4 — later, and now blaming the probes. Slicing section 4 was compelled by that measurement.

### The argument for accepting

Log text cannot distinguish a handled exception from an unhandled one. `@better-auth/oauth-provider` **deliberately** uses the UNIQUE violation as its race-safety mechanism and swallows it at DEBUG; our query engine logs ERROR on the way out, before that caller sees it. Severity was never a sound boot predicate. The root cause — `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` logging at ERROR inside a `catch` that rethrows, which AGENTS.md's *Degradation log levels* names verbatim as wrong — is filed as **#17052**. Once that lands the false ERROR lines are gone at source.

### The risk

Until #17052 lands, a genuinely new error-level boot failure that is not a composition failure passes silently (printed, not red).

### Options

- **A — accept as delivered.** Seat recommendation. Five ablations prove the #16500 specimen, the A2/A3 load sites, the #3091 named signature and the probe-window boundary all still red; the reduction is temporary and #17052 closes it at source.
- **B — more conservative.** Keep "error level fails the boot", plus a maintained white-list of known-benign signatures. ⛔ Cost is exactly the deny-list maintenance both the card and the dev argued against: it decides nothing and the next benign line reopens this.
- **C — sequence it.** Land #17052 first, then #17051. Safest; `publish-smoke / packed-tarballs` stays red meanwhile, so the release instrument stays blind.

### CI state at this reading (2026-09-09T07:5xZ, head `e3c2add9`)

**55 of 56 green.** The single red is ⛔ **not this PR's**: `@objectstack/service-messaging` `plugin-shutdown-stops-dispatchers.test.ts:118` — *"Test timed out in 5000ms"*, 1 failed / 372 passed. This PR touches `scripts/publish-smoke.sh` and one `packages/spec/scripts/` test; `service-messaging` is not in its diff. Handle per the signature ledger before treating it as a defect of #17051.
